reviews.title: Still impressive AM4 in 2026
reviews.comment:
Upgrading from my Ryzen 7 3700 to this Ryzen 9 5900XT was honestly one of the biggest real-world PC upgrades I’ve experienced in a long time. I expected a noticeable improvement, but I was genuinely surprised by just how dramatic the performance jump ended up being across almost everything I do.

The Ryzen 7 3700 was still a solid processor and handled gaming well enough, so I debated for a while whether upgrading on the AM4 platform would really be worth it. After using this CPU for a while now, I can confidently say it absolutely was.

The difference in overall system responsiveness was immediately noticeable the moment I booted into Windows. Applications open faster, multitasking feels effortless, and heavier workloads that used to make my system feel slightly sluggish now barely register. Everything just feels smoother and more immediate.

Gaming performance has been especially impressive. Frame rates are higher and much more stable, particularly in CPU-heavy games and large open-world titles. I also noticed a significant improvement in frame pacing and overall smoothness, especially when multitasking while gaming. I can now have browsers, background apps, monitoring software, and other programs running without feeling like I’m sacrificing performance.

What really impressed me though is how capable this processor is for productivity tasks. The jump from 8 cores to 16 cores and 32 threads makes a huge difference when working with demanding applications. Video rendering, compression tasks, multitasking, and other heavier workloads are dramatically faster now. This CPU absolutely tears through anything I throw at it.

Another huge benefit is that this upgrade allowed me to extend the life of my AM4 platform instead of completely rebuilding my system. I was able to keep my motherboard and DDR4 memory while still getting a massive performance increase. Considering how expensive full platform upgrades can become once you factor in a new motherboard, DDR5 RAM, and everything else, this felt like an incredibly smart upgrade path.

Thermals have also been surprisingly manageable for such a powerful processor. Paired with a good cooler, temperatures have stayed very reasonable even under heavier loads. The processor boosts aggressively when needed but also idles down nicely when the system isn’t under stress.

Installation was straightforward as well. After a BIOS update on my motherboard, the processor dropped right in and worked perfectly. No weird compatibility problems or instability issues. AMD has done a great job keeping AM4 viable for so long, and upgrades like this are exactly why people appreciate the platform.

I also appreciate how well this CPU pairs with modern GPUs. I upgraded my graphics card recently as well, and this processor has no trouble keeping up. It feels like a really balanced high-end setup now without bottlenecking performance.

Overall, this CPU completely exceeded my expectations. The performance increase from the Ryzen 7 3700 was enormous and instantly noticeable in both gaming and productivity. If you’re already on AM4 and looking for a major upgrade without rebuilding your entire PC, this processor is an incredible option. It honestly made my system feel brand new again.

reviews.title: GODLIKE - Enthusiast Level Motherboard!
reviews.comment:
I have built my own PCs using the MSI X870e Tomahawk, Carbon and now the Godlike, and have to say this is a beautiful and well build board. From the moment you see the packaging and unbox it you will notice this is truly a high end and great quality board. It was designed with great aesthetics and truly feels premium from the design, backplate, VRMs, LCD screen, and all the additional cables and accessories included in the box. 

Now, this board is not for everyone, the price is high compared to other X870e motherboards, but you are paying for all the premium and enthusiast level features. I use it for work, ML, AI and gaming, so the features are good for me. I installed all 5 NVME SSD slots, and I am running 2 of them at Gen 5 speeds. You have the ability to add the PCIe accessory and add 2 more NVME SSDs for a total of 7, but you lose from X16 to X8 Gen 5 for your main GPU if you do this, but you have that option. 

The build is different than other mother boards as most connections are on the right of the board, and you need to plan for this, as well as use an extended EATX PC case. You also need to plan and make sure you have the room to connect everything to the right, or you can also use many more ARGB and Fan connections inside your case using the provided hub. 

As you can see on my pictures, this is a great motherboard for custom watercooling, and I used both the pump connections and sensor cables to control my water pumps and keep track of the temps and RPMs. The Godlike LCD looks great as well, and you cna read your sensor data right there, and you can modify it to add images, videos or customize the sensor readings.

In conclusion, this is an excellent motherboard for enthusiast who don't worry about cost, and focus more on Quality, features, looks and push your motherboard to higher limits when overclocking. Have fun with it!

reviews.title: Open Box Excellent Condition Should Mean Working
reviews.comment:
I purchased this ASUS motherboard as an open-box item in "Excellent Condition." When the box arrived, all components were inside and physically looked clean. However, once I started building, the board showed no signs of life. I tested everything outside the case using a screwdriver to jump the power pins. CPU fan spun, power supply turned on, but there were no debug LEDs on the motherboard, nothing at all. I tested with known working RAM, CPU, and GPU. No image, no POST, no power indicators. After thorough troubleshooting, I confirmed the motherboard itself was dead. This is not a review against ASUS, the board may be great when functional. This is about Best Buy's open-box grading. "Excellent Condition" should mean the product is fully functional, not just cosmetically clean. 
If you buy this open-box, test it immediately within the return window. I had to return mine and buy new.

reviews.title: GODLIKE - Enthusiast Level Motherboard!
reviews.comment:
I have built my own PCs using the MSI X870e Tomahawk, Carbon and now the Godlike, and have to say this is a beautiful and well build board. From the moment you see the packaging and unbox it you will notice this is truly a high end and great quality board. It was designed with great aesthetics and truly feels premium from the design, backplate, VRMs, LCD screen, and all the additional cables and accessories included in the box. 

Now, this board is not for everyone, the price is high compared to other X870e motherboards, but you are paying for all the premium and enthusiast level features. I use it for work, ML, AI and gaming, so the features are good for me. I installed all 5 NVME SSD slots, and I am running 2 of them at Gen 5 speeds. You have the ability to add the PCIe accessory and add 2 more NVME SSDs for a total of 7, but you lose from X16 to X8 Gen 5 for your main GPU if you do this, but you have that option. 

The build is different than other mother boards as most connections are on the right of the board, and you need to plan for this, as well as use an extended EATX PC case. You also need to plan and make sure you have the room to connect everything to the right, or you can also use many more ARGB and Fan connections inside your case using the provided hub. 

As you can see on my pictures, this is a great motherboard for custom watercooling, and I used both the pump connections and sensor cables to control my water pumps and keep track of the temps and RPMs. The Godlike LCD looks great as well, and you cna read your sensor data right there, and you can modify it to add images, videos or customize the sensor readings.

In conclusion, this is an excellent motherboard for enthusiast who don't worry about cost, and focus more on Quality, features, looks and push your motherboard to higher limits when overclocking. Have fun with it!

reviews.title: Open Box Excellent Condition Should Mean Working
reviews.comment:
I purchased this ASUS motherboard as an open-box item in "Excellent Condition." When the box arrived, all components were inside and physically looked clean. However, once I started building, the board showed no signs of life. I tested everything outside the case using a screwdriver to jump the power pins. CPU fan spun, power supply turned on, but there were no debug LEDs on the motherboard, nothing at all. I tested with known working RAM, CPU, and GPU. No image, no POST, no power indicators. After thorough troubleshooting, I confirmed the motherboard itself was dead. This is not a review against ASUS, the board may be great when functional. This is about Best Buy's open-box grading. "Excellent Condition" should mean the product is fully functional, not just cosmetically clean. 
If you buy this open-box, test it immediately within the return window. I had to return mine and buy new.

reviews.title: Excellent Board for the Money
reviews.comment:
When I first heard about the new hidden-connector motherboard designs taking over the market, I knew I wanted to build with one.

The Gigabyte X870 Aorus Stealth ICE is honestly one of the nicest hidden-connector boards I have used so far. It looks super clean, has a really strong feature set, feels premium in the hand, and just makes the whole build come together in a way a normal board usually does not.

Design and Aesthetics

The first thing you notice with this board is the look. The all-white color scheme, the white connectors, and the chunky heatsinks all work together really well. If you are going for a clean showcase build, this thing absolutely nails that style.

And obviously, the big selling point is the rear-connector layout. Once everything is built, the front side just looks way cleaner than a traditional motherboard setup. You do still need a case that supports it, and you need to put a little effort into cable management on the back side, but when it all comes together, it looks incredibly clean.

Main Features

As far as features go, this board is stacked. You are getting USB4, Wi-Fi 7, PCIe 5.0 for the graphics card, PCIe 5.0 storage, DDR5 support, and multiple fast M.2 slots. So from a spec standpoint, it definitely feels like a proper high-end AM5 board and not just something that looks good in pictures.

The VRM setup is also really solid with a 16+2+2 twin digital design, which means it has no problem handling higher-end Ryzen CPUs. Pair that with the large heatsinks and the board just feels like it is built for a serious system.
What I also like is that the board is not just about the headline specs. You get four M.2 slots, dual USB4, 5GbE, and the EZ-Latch stuff that makes building a little less annoying. It has a lot of small quality-of-life features that you definitely appreciate once you start putting the system together.

Build Quality

Build quality is one of the areas where this board really stands out. The metal backplate, the large heatsinks, and the debug display all make it feel like a genuinely premium piece of hardware. Even just handling it during the build, it feels sturdy and well thought out instead of flashy but cheap.

Software

On the software side, you are dealing with Gigabyte Control Center.
The good news is that it looks pretty clean and it picked up my RGB right away, which is always nice because that is not something you can take for granted with motherboard software. The downside is that monitoring still feels a little clunky since some of the info is buried in separate sections instead of being right in front of you. It is usable, but there is definitely room for improvement.

Wi-Fi

Wi-Fi was actually one of the more interesting parts of the experience. The board uses a Qualcomm Wi-Fi 7 module with support for 2.4 GHz, 5 GHz, and 6 GHz, plus Bluetooth 5.4, so on paper it is a really strong setup. The only weird part for me was that some of the more advanced stuff, like MLO, was not super obvious in the settings or software.

That said, Wi-Fi 7 only really matters if the rest of your network can take advantage of it, so your router setup is a big part of the story here. I do like that the wireless card is an M.2 module, though, because it means you still have the option to swap it later if you ever want to.

Final Conclusion

So overall, I have been really impressed with the Gigabyte X870 Aorus Stealth ICE. It gives you that super clean hidden-connector look, but it also backs it up with the kind of features and build quality you would expect from a high-end board.

For me, the biggest wins are the design, the overall build quality, the USB4 support, and just how polished the whole thing feels once the system is done. It is the kind of board that makes a lot of sense if you care about performance, but also care a lot about how your build actually looks.

My biggest complaint is still the lane-sharing situation. If you run two PCIe 5.0 M.2 drives, you lose USB4, so if keeping USB4 matters to you, it makes more sense to drop one of those drives into a PCIe 4.0 slot instead.

Pros
•	Super clean hidden-connector layout that makes the finished build look awesome
•	Very solid build quality with a metal backplate and a lot of heatsink coverage
•	Strong modern feature set with USB4, Wi-Fi 7, 5GbE, and PCIe 5.0
•	Nice DIY-friendly features that make the build process easier

Cons
•	Lane sharing can take away USB4 if you install two PCIe 5.0 M.2 drives
•	Some advanced Wi-Fi features are not very clear in the software
•	Gigabyte Control Center still needs a better system monitoring layout
•	You need the right case to really get the most out of the rear-connector design

At the end of the day, this is a really easy board to like if you want a clean AM5 build and still want all the premium stuff.

reviews.title: Potentially good, but a horrible experience!
reviews.comment:
Overall this should, in theory, be an excellent AM5 motherboard for both current and future AMD processors.  It represents good value for a high end AM5 board.  The build quality and features it offers are solid and the included RGB touches add a nice aesthetic.  However, based on my experience I can not recommend this motherboard.

Almost immediately upon utilizing this board I had issues.  Often times the board would not boot properly and would get stuck in a post code loop between error codes 00 and 15.  I managed to get it to post, once or twice, but upon reboot it would get stuck in the same sequence.  I tried multiple different kits of ram, different cpus, a clean windows install, clearing the cmos and flashing the bios.  I know the problem lies with the motherboard as all of the hardware I tried with this board I've tested on another system to make sure they worked properly.

After all of that, and things still not working I RMA'ed the board to MSI to get it fixed.  That process took over a month and when I received the board back it still had the same issues as before.  Frustrated doesn't begin to cover how I felt at that point.  I tried all of the same things I had done previously, before the first RMA, to get the board working properly to no avail.  It is now off in the mail for a second RMA and I don't have any confidence that it will be returned fixed and that I'm going to have to eat the cost of this board.  Unfortunately, as I'm outside of the return window, all I can do is RMA it again and hope it will be fixed or replaced this time.

Additionally, I've read other stories people have posted about MSI's current offerings of AM5 motherboards and how they've had similar issues to my own.  I wish I had checked up on these prior, but up until this point I'd pretty much exclusively used MSI motherboards for my PC builds, going all the way back to the days of AMD FX cpus.  However, that will no longer be the case as this experience has soured me on MSI motherboards.

Lastly, please take this review for what it is, a single person's experience.  I've read plenty of other reviews about how good this motherboard is and I'm sure they aren't wrong.  It seems like I got unlucky and received a bad/buggy one.  I have no doubt that in ideal circumstances these motherboards are excellent and will work just fine, but based on my experience I can't recommend this product.

reviews.title: MSI won me over today
reviews.comment:
After upgrading from my Asus Z690-A Prime, I decided to try the MSI Z890-A WiFi for its modern features and compatibility with Intel's latest processors. As someone accustomed to Asus boards, I was initially hesitant, but MSI has won me over with its exceptional build quality and intuitive BIOS interface. Navigating the menus is straightforward and efficient, making overclocking and system tweaks a seamless experience.

reviews.title: Motherboard of horrors.
reviews.comment:
This motherboard has been a consistently frustrating experience. I updated the BIOS and confirmed that all hardware components were compatible prior to installation. However, from the moment I built my system, issues began to appear. The yellow DRAM light would turn on, Windows would fail to restart properly, and eventually the motherboard stopped functioning. It will not even load into bios now.

I attempted multiple troubleshooting steps, including testing with different RAM and reseating the CPU, but none were successful. Extremely frustrated, I replaced the board with a different brand using the exact same components, and the system booted without any issues.

This motherboard cost me nearly two months of troubleshooting and instability. At this point, I’m unsure if pursuing the RMA process is worth the additional time, effort, and mental drain. I'm just tired of dealing with it and my new board works perfectly.

reviews.title: Potentially good, but a horrible experience!
reviews.comment:
Overall this should, in theory, be an excellent AM5 motherboard for both current and future AMD processors.  It represents good value for a high end AM5 board.  The build quality and features it offers are solid and the included RGB touches add a nice aesthetic.  However, based on my experience I can not recommend this motherboard.

Almost immediately upon utilizing this board I had issues.  Often times the board would not boot properly and would get stuck in a post code loop between error codes 00 and 15.  I managed to get it to post, once or twice, but upon reboot it would get stuck in the same sequence.  I tried multiple different kits of ram, different cpus, a clean windows install, clearing the cmos and flashing the bios.  I know the problem lies with the motherboard as all of the hardware I tried with this board I've tested on another system to make sure they worked properly.

After all of that, and things still not working I RMA'ed the board to MSI to get it fixed.  That process took over a month and when I received the board back it still had the same issues as before.  Frustrated doesn't begin to cover how I felt at that point.  I tried all of the same things I had done previously, before the first RMA, to get the board working properly to no avail.  It is now off in the mail for a second RMA and I don't have any confidence that it will be returned fixed and that I'm going to have to eat the cost of this board.  Unfortunately, as I'm outside of the return window, all I can do is RMA it again and hope it will be fixed or replaced this time.

Additionally, I've read other stories people have posted about MSI's current offerings of AM5 motherboards and how they've had similar issues to my own.  I wish I had checked up on these prior, but up until this point I'd pretty much exclusively used MSI motherboards for my PC builds, going all the way back to the days of AMD FX cpus.  However, that will no longer be the case as this experience has soured me on MSI motherboards.

Lastly, please take this review for what it is, a single person's experience.  I've read plenty of other reviews about how good this motherboard is and I'm sure they aren't wrong.  It seems like I got unlucky and received a bad/buggy one.  I have no doubt that in ideal circumstances these motherboards are excellent and will work just fine, but based on my experience I can't recommend this product.

reviews.comment:

⸻

I’ve been using the ASUS Prime RTX 5070 for a while now, and overall I’m really impressed with its performance and build quality.

The card feels solid and well-built right out of the box. ASUS did a great job with the design—it’s sturdy without being overly bulky, and it fits nicely into my setup. One of the biggest highlights for me is how quiet it runs. Even under load, the fans stay surprisingly low-noise, which makes a big difference during long gaming or work sessions.

Performance-wise, it handles modern games very smoothly. I’ve had no issues running titles at high settings, and frame rates stay consistent without noticeable drops. It’s a reliable card if you want a good balance between performance and efficiency.

I also use it for running local AI models, and it performs really well there too. Inference is fast, and it handles workloads without struggling, which makes it a great option if you’re doing both gaming and AI-related tasks on the same machine.

Overall, I’d say this GPU is a solid choice if you’re looking for something quiet, well-built, and capable across both gaming and AI workloads.

reviews.title: Only get is you need cuda and the vram
reviews.comment: I bought this GPU about a month ago. I run Linux on my computer and use CUDA. The vram is great when I am running some MD simulations and some LLM workloads. Previously owning a 4090 and a 5080, this card is a powerhouse. For my workloads I played around with the power limits and clocks. Surprisingly I was able to retain the majority of the compute throughput (90-95% on some workloads) by lowering the power from 575W down to 400W. Dialing in the specs of this card really does make this card shine for my work. However, I did keep records of my past GPUs and this current one. On a performance/compute per watt/cuda core/dollar, the 5080 was the best bang for my buck. I probably should have kept the 4090, and saved myself a lot of money. Or I ought to have bought the 5090 back in October of 2025. Regardless, I needed the vram and the cuda compute so I bit the bullet and purchase the 5090. I would really recommend the 5090 for those that would use the vram and use nvidias core functionalities. Something to keep in mind is that the MSI 5090 is a monster card. I did not want the power cable to bend/kink when I put the glass panel, so I bought a vertical GPU mount to keep it all contained. The case is a 5000x, so this GPU is massive.

reviews.title: All the performance without the bling
reviews.comment: The PNY RTX 5080 OC is an absolute sleeper card once you toss out the stock settings and actually tune the silicon with an undervolt and overclock. While it ships as a basic, no-frills model, it clearly has tons of hidden headroom. Dropping the core voltage down 0.975mV while locking the core clock at a flat 3100MHz completely changes the efficiency profile. It bypasses the aggressive voltage-frequency curve that causes these modern cards to pull unnecessary wattage and dump massive heat into the case. Combined with +2000MHz memory clock offset, the expanded bandwidth allows the GPU to sustain those high clocks under heavy 4K loads without hitting power or thermal limits. The fans actually run at a reasonable RPM because the undervolt keeps the hotspot temperatures well within check, usually running around 62c while gaming in a well ventilated case and room temps in the low 70s. Pairing this GPU with the Ryzen 7 9800X3D removes any remaining bottlenecks. The massive 3D V-Cache on the 9800X3D keeps the frame render queue entirely full, resulting in a perfectly flat frametime graph with practically nonexistent micro-stutters. Even in simulation-heavy titles or unoptimized open-world engines that normally choke a CPU, the 1% lows remain incredibly high. Whether you are running native path tracing or pushing a high-refresh-rate panel, this hardware combination handles everything effortlessly. The only negative is the current pricing environment of PC parts, all things considered though, I would buy this GPU again.

reviews.title: Vengeance DDR5 32GB review
reviews.comment:
The first time I went into the store to buy laptop memory, I told the sales person I was looking for memory for my gaming laptop. However, I made a mistake and didn't say "gaming laptop", instead mentioned the model of my laptop. I was fairly inexperienced with buying memory for a laptop, so I accepted the item the sales person recommended. Well, the problem was, they didn't ask additional questions to confirm exactly what kind of memory I needed, and instead by memory sticks for a PC. As soon as I got home, and opened it up, I realized the mistake and had to return it of course. I returned it, and bout the correct stick of ram, but again, when I asked the sales person about options, they just grabbed 1 32GB stick. After I got home, opened the laptop, and realized there was two slots I could put memory in, I did a little research on line, and found that due to dual channel it is better to have 2 16GB of ram, than 1 32GB. So, I returned to the store, and returned it and got 2 16 GB sticks. The first thing I would say about this review is, Best Buy, you would save yourself money with returns, by making sure your sales people be a little more inquisitive, and help the customer confirm exactly what they need and want. 

 
Unfortunately, after all of that, and getting the 2 sticks of 16GB ram installed, it still didn't boost my gaming laptop enough to handle what I was trying to do with some VR modding. To pay over $400 for just 32GBs of ram and it not boost performance enough is why I gave this product 2 starts, and because of the lack of expert help at Best Buy.

Highly recommend.

reviews.title: Was sent WRONG product (4) times!
reviews.comment:
I ordered (2) sets of this Corsair 64GB DDR5 CL30 non-RGB & was sent 2 sets of 32GB DDR5 CL36 RGB. (!) To make matters worse, the packages appeared opened / tampered with & appeared to have some sort of wrong memory swapped in place of the Corsair. 

Because I needed these sets in a timely fashion for a new customer build, I called customer service & they sent out (2) replacements which were also wrong! At least these 2 packages appear new / unopened / & like they are the actual Corsair RAM they are supposed to be in the packaging. The problem is they are not the RAM sticks I ordered, but are rather HALF the RAM (32GB instead of 64GB & slower CL of 36 instead of 30…+ they have RGB whereas the sticks I ordered need to be the lower profile non-RGB). This is complete insanity! I’ve never had an order messed up by Best Buy like this…multiple times in a row with the same product being mixed up almost feels like I’m being punked. 

So now I’ll have to waste an hour drive time each way + the time spent in store (guaranteed it’ll take at least an hour to get it solved) to our nearest Best Buy to try to straighten this out (as I don’t trust it’ll be handled correctly if I do all the returns via mail). 

Mind boggling.

reviews.title: Perfect Value SSD
reviews.comment:
I bought this SSD specifically to expand the storage in my Eufy HomeBase 3, and so far it has been completely reliable. I spent a lot of time researching compatible drives before purchasing because I wanted something dependable that I could basically install and forget about. After using Samsung SSDs in computers over the years, this one felt like a safe choice, and it has absolutely lived up to that reputation.

Installation into the HomeBase 3 was extremely simple. The drive slid right into place, mounted without any issues, and was recognized immediately by the system. I honestly expected there to be at least some sort of formatting or compatibility hiccup, but everything worked smoothly right out of the box. Within just a few minutes, the extra storage was available and recording properly.

One thing I really appreciate is the peace of mind this drive provides. Since my Eufy system handles security cameras around my home, reliability matters much more to me than chasing benchmark numbers or squeezing out a few extra megabytes per second. I needed something stable that could handle continuous recording without random disconnects, errors, or overheating issues. This drive has done exactly that.

Since installing it, I haven’t had a single issue with dropped footage, drive errors, or weird behavior from the HomeBase. Playback loads quickly, clips save properly, and recordings remain accessible without lag or buffering. The whole system just feels smooth and responsive.

Samsung drives have always had a strong reputation for reliability, and this SSD reminds me why people trust them so much. Even though the HomeBase 3 doesn’t necessarily need the fastest SSD on the market, it’s nice knowing there’s quality hardware inside handling all the recordings in the background. It gives me confidence that my footage is actually being stored safely.

Another nice surprise was how cool and quiet the drive runs. Obviously SSDs are already silent, but temperature stability was something I paid attention to because the HomeBase can stay active constantly with multiple cameras connected. Even with ongoing recordings and motion events throughout the day, the drive has remained stable without any overheating concerns.

The 1TB size has also been a really good balance for my setup. It gives me significantly more recording space without going overboard on cost. Depending on your camera count and recording settings, this amount of storage can go a surprisingly long way. For me, it was the perfect middle ground between affordability and capacity.

I also appreciate how mature SATA SSDs have become in general. They may not be as flashy as newer NVMe drives, but for devices like the Eufy HomeBase 3, a dependable SATA SSD honestly makes a lot of sense. They are proven, stable, and easy to work with.

Overall, this has been exactly the kind of upgrade I was hoping for. Simple installation, excellent compatibility with the Eufy HomeBase 3, reliable operation, and zero headaches since setup. Sometimes the best compliment you can give a storage device is that you completely forget about it because it just quietly works in the background every single day. That has been my experience with this Samsung 870 EVO.

reviews.title: Mixed Thoughts on these Hard Drive Purchases
reviews.comment: I'm somewhere in the middle on the overall rating for this hard drive. We purchased several and some arrived with physical damage (small dents), others that don't even work, and finally ones that work great thus far. I've read that Seagate does not warranty physical damage, like the dents describe above, so you will want to return those for a new hard drive. The jury is still out on the hard drives that are physically in good condition and show "success" in the S.M.A.R.T drive report. On sale, this is a great value per TB, but I can't speak on the longevity yet. Finally, I do have 18TB Ironwolf Pro drives and they are still spinning 5+ years later so I would recommend this brand, but please beware that you may receive physically damaged drives and also non-working drives upon arrival. This in turn is going to be a hassle to exchange/return, especially if you got them on sale, cashback, etc.. Fingers crossed that the drives that are working and in physically good condition, last for many years to come!

reviews.title: Perfect Value SSD
reviews.comment:
I bought this SSD specifically to expand the storage in my Eufy HomeBase 3, and so far it has been completely reliable. I spent a lot of time researching compatible drives before purchasing because I wanted something dependable that I could basically install and forget about. After using Samsung SSDs in computers over the years, this one felt like a safe choice, and it has absolutely lived up to that reputation.

Installation into the HomeBase 3 was extremely simple. The drive slid right into place, mounted without any issues, and was recognized immediately by the system. I honestly expected there to be at least some sort of formatting or compatibility hiccup, but everything worked smoothly right out of the box. Within just a few minutes, the extra storage was available and recording properly.

One thing I really appreciate is the peace of mind this drive provides. Since my Eufy system handles security cameras around my home, reliability matters much more to me than chasing benchmark numbers or squeezing out a few extra megabytes per second. I needed something stable that could handle continuous recording without random disconnects, errors, or overheating issues. This drive has done exactly that.

Since installing it, I haven’t had a single issue with dropped footage, drive errors, or weird behavior from the HomeBase. Playback loads quickly, clips save properly, and recordings remain accessible without lag or buffering. The whole system just feels smooth and responsive.

Samsung drives have always had a strong reputation for reliability, and this SSD reminds me why people trust them so much. Even though the HomeBase 3 doesn’t necessarily need the fastest SSD on the market, it’s nice knowing there’s quality hardware inside handling all the recordings in the background. It gives me confidence that my footage is actually being stored safely.

Another nice surprise was how cool and quiet the drive runs. Obviously SSDs are already silent, but temperature stability was something I paid attention to because the HomeBase can stay active constantly with multiple cameras connected. Even with ongoing recordings and motion events throughout the day, the drive has remained stable without any overheating concerns.

The 1TB size has also been a really good balance for my setup. It gives me significantly more recording space without going overboard on cost. Depending on your camera count and recording settings, this amount of storage can go a surprisingly long way. For me, it was the perfect middle ground between affordability and capacity.

I also appreciate how mature SATA SSDs have become in general. They may not be as flashy as newer NVMe drives, but for devices like the Eufy HomeBase 3, a dependable SATA SSD honestly makes a lot of sense. They are proven, stable, and easy to work with.

Overall, this has been exactly the kind of upgrade I was hoping for. Simple installation, excellent compatibility with the Eufy HomeBase 3, reliable operation, and zero headaches since setup. Sometimes the best compliment you can give a storage device is that you completely forget about it because it just quietly works in the background every single day. That has been my experience with this Samsung 870 EVO.

reviews.author: NickM

reviews.title: Perfect Value SSD
reviews.comment:
I bought this SSD specifically to expand the storage in my Eufy HomeBase 3, and so far it has been completely reliable. I spent a lot of time researching compatible drives before purchasing because I wanted something dependable that I could basically install and forget about. After using Samsung SSDs in computers over the years, this one felt like a safe choice, and it has absolutely lived up to that reputation.

Installation into the HomeBase 3 was extremely simple. The drive slid right into place, mounted without any issues, and was recognized immediately by the system. I honestly expected there to be at least some sort of formatting or compatibility hiccup, but everything worked smoothly right out of the box. Within just a few minutes, the extra storage was available and recording properly.

One thing I really appreciate is the peace of mind this drive provides. Since my Eufy system handles security cameras around my home, reliability matters much more to me than chasing benchmark numbers or squeezing out a few extra megabytes per second. I needed something stable that could handle continuous recording without random disconnects, errors, or overheating issues. This drive has done exactly that.

Since installing it, I haven’t had a single issue with dropped footage, drive errors, or weird behavior from the HomeBase. Playback loads quickly, clips save properly, and recordings remain accessible without lag or buffering. The whole system just feels smooth and responsive.

Samsung drives have always had a strong reputation for reliability, and this SSD reminds me why people trust them so much. Even though the HomeBase 3 doesn’t necessarily need the fastest SSD on the market, it’s nice knowing there’s quality hardware inside handling all the recordings in the background. It gives me confidence that my footage is actually being stored safely.

Another nice surprise was how cool and quiet the drive runs. Obviously SSDs are already silent, but temperature stability was something I paid attention to because the HomeBase can stay active constantly with multiple cameras connected. Even with ongoing recordings and motion events throughout the day, the drive has remained stable without any overheating concerns.

The 1TB size has also been a really good balance for my setup. It gives me significantly more recording space without going overboard on cost. Depending on your camera count and recording settings, this amount of storage can go a surprisingly long way. For me, it was the perfect middle ground between affordability and capacity.

I also appreciate how mature SATA SSDs have become in general. They may not be as flashy as newer NVMe drives, but for devices like the Eufy HomeBase 3, a dependable SATA SSD honestly makes a lot of sense. They are proven, stable, and easy to work with.

Overall, this has been exactly the kind of upgrade I was hoping for. Simple installation, excellent compatibility with the Eufy HomeBase 3, reliable operation, and zero headaches since setup. Sometimes the best compliment you can give a storage device is that you completely forget about it because it just quietly works in the background every single day. That has been my experience with this Samsung 870 EVO.

reviews.title: Zero regrets after months of heavy use on my Ryzen
reviews.comment:
I’ve been running this Samsung 9100 PRO since October because I wanted to see how it held up before reporting back. My only real regret is that I didn’t buy two of them while I was at it.

I’m using this with a Ryzen 9950X and an X870E motherboard, and the speeds are absolutely top-tier. I had some "crucial" stability issues with a drive from another vendor, but this Samsung has been flawless. The Samsung Magician software made cloning my old drive a breeze with zero errors.

The heatsink does its job well, though my only minor complaint is that it's not meant to be removed, which makes the motherboard look a bit different—but my GPU blocks the view anyway, so it doesn't matter. Huge shout out to the Augusta, Maine Best Buy team for a much better experience than my recent online orders elsewhere!

The biggest highlight for me is the airflow. My system stays cooler, and the case feels like it was actually designed with performance in mind, not just looks. At the same time, the RGB fans and glass panel make the whole setup look sharp without being too flashy.

Another thing I really liked was how easy it was to build in. There’s plenty of room to work, cable management is much easier, and the final result looks clean and professional. It made the whole build experience smoother and less frustrating.

Overall, this is one of the best-looking and most functional cases I’ve purchased. It gives you strong airflow, great presentation, and a very clean setup. I would definitely recommend it to anyone building a gaming or high-performance PC.

reviews.title: My All-White Build’s New Star Case
reviews.comment:
I just upgraded to the NZXT H9 Flow+ RGB 2025 in white and it totally changed my build — not just in look, but in feel. The clean white frame + wraparound tempered glass lets every bit of my hardware shine through, and the included RGB fans add just the right touch of color without clashing. The dual-chamber design made cable management so much easier; hiding the PSU space and drives keeps the main side super clean. Airflow is top-tier — perforated panels, angled fan intake, and support for big radiators (up to 420mm) means temps stay cool even under load.

Putting this case in my setup was one of the best choices: it makes everything look premium, crisp, and cohesive. If you're working with a white build and want something that shows off your components, keeps things cool, and looks sharp, this case is absolutely worth it.

reviews.title: Make no mistake, its big
reviews.comment:
Just make sure you are going into this case understanding its size well.

The new Frame cases from Corsair are slightly bigger in every way compared to the previous versions.

Now, to be honest I was not going to really write this review until I Corsair came through with their promises of the modular add-ons to customize the case to your liking.

They recently released a bunch of new front grills, side panel, motherboard tray and PSU cover options, I can say that this is now a fully fleshed out product.  

As the product stands on its own, its good.  Its high airflow, its quite simple yet attractive at the same time.  Yes, it does seem like its a plain case, but there are so many options to be had in the 5000.  You have three 360 radiator options, up to 12 120mm fans, any CPU air cooler should fit in this beast.

The only points I can really take away from the case is that the stock panels do feel a little "cheap" and I mean for the price of the FRAME cases, I don't think I can be too harsh.  In a time when everything is expensive, being able to get your hands on a case with a much versatility as the FRAME cases, is actually great.

I think overall this is a 5 star product, especially now with all the new panels that are being offered.  If you are not interested in any of those, then this is a solid 4 star case with only points off for the lower quality side panels that come with it.  Pure performance wise, this case will not let you down.

All the screws are just haphazardly thrown into bags together instead of seperated and labeled at all. Install guide is complete garbage that SOMEBODY could have put at least a bit of effort into helping first time builders. Have to akwardly bend your hdmi, dp, and usb cables to fit into the mobo and gpu slots before putting the top of the case back on (also causing my 2nd monitor to barely reach). (Clips actually next to the fan mounts would be great for holding loose hanging daisy chains). Between the busted cheap fans and the support bracket not fitting i of course emailed thermaltake support about warranty and have not heard back days later. Best buy support in the app assured me I could go to my local store and have them at least replace the fans with the same model (the store did NOT). It's a little unclear from the images, but the top panel pops off to expose the mobo's I/O shield, and cables can route through a couple of holes in the back. I have a wifi antenna and HDMI cable running out of mine and there's enough room between the plugs and the top panel so that the cables aren't squished down or anything. Like I said, plenty of room.

This was delivered from the manufacturer in the original box that includes product images on the sides, and could easily be mistaken for a computer by any porch pirates, so keep that in mind. The packaging inside was fine and my unit had no damage issues.

reviews.title: The Best-Looking AIO Money Can Buy (But Your Walle
reviews.comment:
The Kraken Elite 360mm is basically the cool kid of CPU coolers—literally and figuratively. The new 2.72-inch IPS screen is gorgeous, way brighter and bigger than before, and throwing a custom GIF on there never gets old . Cooling performance is legit too—NZXT ditched Asetek for their own "Turbine" pump, and it keeps high-end chips like the 7800X3D or 14900K surprisingly chilly even under load . Installation is straightforward with pre-applied paste and a single breakout cable, so you won't be cursing at your motherboard for an hour .

That said, it's not all smooth sailing. The CAM software is the usual love-it-or-hate-it situation—cool when it works, annoying when it bugs out or feels bloated . The price stings too; you're paying a premium for that screen more than raw cooling performance . Also, some users have reported pump noise or software glitches over time, so reliability isn't a sure thing . If you want the best-looking AIO on the block and don't mind the cost, go for it. If you just care about thermals, a cheaper Arctic Liquid Freezer III will get you 90% of the way there for half the cash.

The good:

Runs surprisingly quietly under most use cases.
Even when the CPU is being hammered, the noise level is very low.
The bad:
The "instruction" sheet is nearly entirely useless other than identifying which pieces of metal are needed for which CPU type.

---

If I wasn't an electronics technician by trade this AIO would likely have been returned due to the paucity of the instructions. As it was, it took far more thinking and fiddling than one should reasonably expect from a (relatively) non-technical component.

I'd recommend this item to someone with a high level of technical skill and comfort level; or for somebody for whom I'd be available to answer (the inevitable) questions.

reviews.title: Screen DOA
reviews.comment:
I have pretty mixed feelings about this cooler because the actual cooling performance has been excellent, but the experience getting everything fully working was much more frustrating than it should have been.

The biggest issue is that the LCD screen was completely dead right out of the box. Unfortunately, the screen was one of the main reasons I specifically purchased this version instead of a standard AIO cooler, so opening everything up, installing it, and realizing the display wouldn’t turn on at all was incredibly disappointing. The pump itself worked, the fans spun normally, and cooling performance was fine, but the LCD module was totally DOA.

To CORSAIR’s credit, their customer service was ultimately good to work with, but the process felt far more drawn out and complicated than necessary. Initially, they wanted me to remove the entire cooler from my system and mail the whole thing back. That would have meant removing the radiator, fans, thermal paste, and basically tearing apart a freshly completed build over what was clearly just a failed LCD module.

After some back and forth, I explained that the screen itself is removable and that CORSAIR literally sells the LCD module separately as its own standalone product. Once they understood that, they finally agreed to just send me a replacement screen instead of requiring me to return the entire unit. That was definitely the correct solution, but it took longer than I expected to get there.

There was also a bit of frustration regarding shipping costs. At first they wanted me to pay for postage, which honestly didn’t sit well considering the part arrived defective from day one. Thankfully, after additional communication, they eventually provided a prepaid shipping label and handled it properly. Again, they made it right in the end, but the overall process could have been much smoother.

Now for the actual cooler itself, because outside of the LCD issue, it has honestly been fantastic.

Cooling performance has been excellent on my system. Temperatures stay low even under heavy gaming and productivity workloads, and the pump and fans are impressively quiet. I was expecting a 360mm cooler to perform well, but I’ve still been pleasantly surprised with how efficiently this thing handles heat while remaining relatively silent.

Installation itself was also pretty straightforward. The mounting hardware felt solid, the pre-applied thermal paste made setup easier, and the daisy-chained fan connections helped reduce cable clutter significantly. Once installed, it gives the system a really clean look overall.

After receiving the replacement screen, the LCD functionality has worked perfectly. The display is vibrant, sharp, and very customizable through iCUE software. I really enjoy being able to display CPU temperatures, GIFs, and custom images directly on the pump head. It adds a lot of personality to the build and honestly looks great once everything is functioning properly.

The software customization is fairly easy as well. I had no trouble setting up screen layouts, animations, and monitoring information. The display quality itself exceeded my expectations once I finally got a working module.

Overall, this cooler performs extremely well and looks fantastic when fully functional. The only reason this experience was frustrating was because the LCD screen arrived dead and the RMA process took longer than necessary. Still, CORSAIR did eventually make things right, and since getting the replacement screen installed, the cooler has been reliable and issue-free.

If you're building a high-end rig and want fans that deliver both form and function, this kit is a no-brainer. Corsair continues to raise the bar for smart cooling solutions.

reviews.title: Excellent Aesthetics Option - Same Great Build
reviews.comment:
I returned after realizing I had the correct fan (not reversed) originally.  The reverse blades, however, are very nice (I have two 140mm Reversed Blade Corsair Fans installed).

These fans are very nice.  Well built, great aesthetic appeal, quiet, and move a lot of air.  The "Time Warp" lighting function is very attractive.  iCue software is easy enough to use.  The fans snap together easily with a passive and active connector and feel stable.  The Daisy-chaining solution of the Corsair fans is very clean, but can be tight and limit orientation depending on case size.  The iCue System Hub I found to be an unreliable/sensitive part.  Of the units installed, 4/7 hubs would not work or failed during installations/setup (included with starter packs).

Overall, I am very pleased with Corsair fans.

Any fans touching, so these 3 fans are magnetized and snap together, then out of one end it is a singular cable that connects to your next chain of fans - all the way to the end of the line, which is a small adapter/hub in the back of your PC. 

Will be very hard to go back to using any other fans after this. I have bought about 20, both computers using nothing but the Icue Link fans.

The LX themselves look great, the reverse blade cleans up the entire look, and leaves your RGB front and center. Great fans, but pricey.

reviews.title: Utter Trash
reviews.comment:
Received the monitor the next unboxed it and immediately the stryfoam goes all over the place. Set up the monitor and immediately found the screw to connect the stand to the base was missing. Annoying, but I emailed support. They wanted a photo, which I couldn't provide through the Best Buy portal, so I explained the situation in writing and they said they'd send it. It's the only screw that's supposed to come in the box. 

I needed a monitor, so I drove to a hardware store to improvise while the correct screw shipped. Spent an hour finding the right one.

Got home, used the improvised screw, set up the stand, plugged everything in, and the monitor wouldn't detect my computer. Never had this issue before despite similar exact same setup with different monitor at two homes! Two hours of troubleshooting later, I finally got it working. Image quality was immediately disappointing. Adjusted every setting available and couldn't fix it. You get what you pay for, I suppose.

While waiting for the replacement screw, I ordered a monitor arm. The VESA housing didn't fit. Assumed I had the wrong arm, ordered another. Replacement screws arrived -- also wrong. 

Bought a new monitor arm, but due to timing had to ship it to my other house and bring it back to this location. Set it up, and the VESA housing still didn't fit. On closer inspection, there's a physical imperfection in the housing itself.... the last straw. 

I returned it but Deca Brands owes me three hours of my life back.

reviews.title: Is not worth it for the long run
reviews.comment:
I am not a purchaser of this product through Best Buy, however, I was a backer through the original Kickstarter campaign and received my monitors in February 2023. 

A few months ago, the top monitor to my base Geminos developed a streak of shadow vertically through the monitor and a constant high-pitched noise that was not too loud but always present and loud enough while working to be a clear distraction. I reached out to Mobile Pixels and asked if they could fix it and they said even though I was a backer to this project that the monitor was out of warranty and they could only fix it through a fee. Fine, the problems didn't make the monitors inoperable and I could work through the noise with basically any cheap headphones. Just yesterday, the top monitor got extremely worse. Constantly turned off, then when it was on there was either glaring blue pixel problems plaguing the screen, then constant green flashes and glitches across the entire monitor, making it entirely broken. The bottom monitor working perfectly as expected just made this entire process even worse because I could see the potential of both monitors being a perfect work-from-home companion that doesn't take a lot of desk space. Incredibly disappointed with this project, would not recommend Geminos to anyone if this is what happens less than two years of owning the monitors, and the lack of care from Mobile Pixels to help repair their own products from confirmed backers that helped get these off ground in the first place.

reviews.title: Wish it worked out for me
reviews.comment:
This might be a 5-star monitor for some, but unfortunately, it didn't work out for me. I loved the clean, chinless design with no branding on the front. I loved the amount of connectivity--that pop-down hub on the left is so useful, and the Ethernet is a great extra feature. I loved having 120hz. The panel had no backlight bleed and felt very uniform. The KVM worked quickly to swap between my PC and my Macbook.

But for whatever reason, the monitor gave me awful eye strain. I tried everything--adjusting height, distance, brightness, contrast, scaling, and nothing seemed to help. Most of the strain seemed to come while using my Mac, and I learned that 4K does not scale properly within MacOS, leading to slightly blurry edges. Because my primary use-case for this monitor is text and writing (I stare at words for many hours a day), this was not acceptable. I've since changed to an Asus 5K monitor, and the improvement in clarity is obvious. 

Text is crisp and scaled properly within Windows, so if you are a PC user, this monitor will probably be fine for you. But some Mac users, particularly those who need perfect clarity, may have issues.  I also experienced the dreaded "coil whine" issue after about a week of use, and it's not nearly as bad as some people make it out to be if you don't share a bedroom with your computer. However, for something of this price, I would expect better quality control.

I do recommend the monitor, because I'm sure it will work great for most people.

reviews.title: Great if you need a small monitor
reviews.comment:
Overall – This is a great little monitor.  It quietly does almost everything right. Dell took a lot of key items - IPS color, 144Hz refresh, FreeSync, adjustable stand – and packed them into an everyday use monitor that works in office and home environments.  If you have limited desk space or just need something extra with a laptop, it’s great. That said, it is a bit small for everyday use. 
Packaging – Dell seems to have this figured out. It’s well-protected with everything neatly organized. Nothing fancy, but everything secure, clearly labeled, and ready to go. 

Assembly – Assembly is a strong point here. Tool-less setup, the stand clicks together easily, and the monitor snaps right in place. Take it out of the box, screw the base on, and snap it into place – took me more time to get the HDMI plugged in than to put it together. 

Touch and Feel – Dell kept the design clean and professional. Thin bezels make it look modern, and the stand is actually better than what you normally get in this class—height, tilt, and swivel adjustments instead of the usual tilt-only budget stand. It doesn’t feel like a $500 monitor, but it does not feel cheap by any means. 

Setup & Functionality – The IPS panel gives good color accuracy and wide viewing angles, text is crisp, and the 144Hz refresh makes everything—from spreadsheets to gaming—feel noticeably smoother. FreeSync worked OK, there was no noticeable shutter.  I used it for about 4 hours straight and did not notice any eye fatigue that I experienced from the smaller footprint.  Awitch between inputs was easy and straightforward, as were all of the other monitor settings – exactly what I would expect from Dell.

It’s nice to see them expand to 2 HDMI ports; however, a display or usbc would have been nice and maybe added some extra flexibility.  The only other drawback is that I may be spoiled with my standard setup of OLED monitors, but the IPS panel doesn’t get the black right – it’s more of a dark gray.  I did notice a bit of motion smoothing, but not significant. 
I
f you have limited desk space or just a little extra for a laptop, I would highly recommend this – not sure there’s much better at this point.  However, for me and usual set up of 34in coupled with a 27in or dual 32ins the 24in did feel a bit small.

Picture this: you're a gamer and your primary screen is your 15" laptop screen, with a 21" monitor streaming YouTube next to you.  Skibbidi, right?  Now, refresh and picture the update: you're a gamer and your primary screen is a 27" Dell HD 144Hz widescreen.  Now you have that main character energy!

In fact, when spinning left to right, or right to left, the bottom 1/3 of the screen seems to "split" from the top 2/3 and lags behind.  The lag isn't enough to get a character in trouble, but it's noticeable in the heat of the game.  It's happened in multiple games, too, so it's not the specific software.  

Setup was straightforward with a power cable and the HDMI.  I would have preferred a D-port connection over HDMI, but if you're hooking it up to older equipment, HDMI works just fine.  The physical buttons are conveniently located, and the computer didn't have any issues locating the new monitor.

For the price point, it's a decent monitor, but don't expect too much from it as it's not a 4K UHD Nvidia DLSS-equipped setup that can fully utilize ray-tracing.  If you're looking for size, this monitor definitely delivers, especially at this price point.

reviews.title: A Solid Everyday Monitor With a Few Gotchas
reviews.comment:
Refresh Rate Reality Check: The 144Hz That… Isn’t

On paper, this 27" Dell monitor promises a 144Hz refresh rate, which sounds great - until you look at the ports. Since it only includes HDMI 1.4, you can’t reliably hit that full 144Hz. Modern DisplayPort handles high refresh rates effortlessly, but HDMI 1.4 tends to tap out closer to 120Hz unless you’re using the newest HDMI 2.2 hardware and cables.

Because Dell skipped DisplayPort entirely on this model, the advertised 144Hz ends up being more of a “nice idea” than something most users will actually experience. If you’re buying this specifically for high-refresh gaming, that’s a meaningful limitation to know upfront.

Resolution & Panel Quality: Great for Work, Not Built for Pros or Competitive Gamers

The SE2726HS runs at 1080p, which is perfectly fine for everyday use - browsing, spreadsheets, schoolwork, general productivity. For that crowd, it looks clean and sharp enough.

But if you’re a competitive gamer chasing every pixel of clarity or a content creator who needs precise detail, 1080p on a 27" screen isn’t going to cut it. You’ll probably want something sharper or more color-accurate.

The IPS panel itself is solid. Colors stay consistent from different angles, which is great for office setups or shared workspaces. It’s not a color-grading monitor and it’s not trying to be - so while it won’t wow professional creatives, it handles day-to-day tasks beautifully.

One nice bonus: AMD FreeSync. It does a great job reducing screen tearing in games that support it, which helps smooth out the overall experience even if the panel isn’t built for high-end gaming.

Final Verdict: Who This Monitor Is Actually For

The Dell SE2726HS is a straightforward, dependable monitor that does exactly what most people need it to do. The picture is clean, the colors are decent, and it’s comfortable to use for long work sessions. For the price, it’s genuinely a strong value - especially for students, professionals, or anyone who just wants a reliable display without spending a fortune.

If you’re expecting OLED-level visuals or a cutting-edge gaming experience, this isn’t the monitor for you. But if you want something practical, affordable, and easy to live with, the SE2726HS fits the bill nicely. It’s not my favorite monitor ever, but it’s definitely not a bad one either. For everyday tasks, it gets the job done without fuss.

reviews.title: Premium Quality Cable That Completes the Build
reviews.comment:
I've been upgrading my rig and wanted a clean, efficient, and durable solution for powering my new NVIDIA GPU. The CORSAIR 12-Pin GPU Power Cable (Sleeved - Black) exceeded expectations on every front.

Build Quality:
First off, the sleeving is top-notch. It feels sturdy without being overly rigid, and the black color blends in seamlessly with the rest of my components for a sleek, minimalist look. The cable is clearly made from high-quality materials and shows no signs of fraying or wear even after a few bends during installation.

Performance:
Functionally, it's flawless. It delivers clean and stable power to the GPU with no issues at all. I’m running a high-end 40-series card, and the connection is snug and secure with no looseness. I’ve seen no thermal or power anomalies since installing it.

Aesthetics & Fit:
This is where Corsair shines. The sleeving gives the cable a premium, custom look that really elevates the build. If you're using a Corsair PSU and want to avoid bulky adapters, this cable is a clean and elegant solution. The cable length is also just right for proper cable management in a mid-to-full tower case.

Compatibility:
It’s a perfect match for Corsair modular PSUs and plugs directly into the PSU side without any need for converters. Be sure to check compatibility (it works with Type 4 PSUs), but if you're in the Corsair ecosystem, it's essentially plug-and-play.

Bottom Line:
This cable is a must-have if you're running a modern GPU and want a clean look without sacrificing performance or reliability. It's a small investment that makes a big difference in both aesthetics and system stability. Highly recommended for anyone doing a custom build or a GPU upgrade.
